newsitem.title: GERMANY: German hostage-taker arrested, captives unharmed.
newsitem.headline: German hostage-taker arrested, captives unharmed.

text.p: An armed man holding six people hostage in a southwest German bank gave himself up on Saturday and freed all of his captives unharmed, police said.
The man had been arrested at the scene in Neuenstein, near Heidelberg, and more details would be given at a news conference later, a police spokesman said.

The man had taken the three men and three women hostage on Friday afternoon, apparently after his attempt to rob the bank went wrong, and demanded a ransom of five million marks ($3 million) and a getaway car in return for their safe release.
Police had brought the money and the car to the scene in the early hours of Saturday morning but negotiations with the man continued throughout the night.
At one point, police negoiators heard 10 shots being fired as they talked with the man by telephone. They said they believed the hostages had not been hit.
Police said they believed the man may be known to them but declined to give any further details. Voice analysis experts said they thought he was aged about 30.
